page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-1200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical AMD EPYC cores with multithreading enabled. The system operates on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate strong CPU capabilities, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng performance placing in the top 25%. Geekbench testing corroborates this with a single-core score of 1994.0 and a multi-core score of 16954.0, alongside strong performance in image and text processing. Memory performance is stable, with uncached large-block read bandwidth at 141.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 71.93 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance remain in the average tier, with Redis handling 42.05 million operations per second.

Given the high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC cores, this server offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The combination of dedicated compute resources, substantial RAM, and fast local NVMe storage makes this instance highly suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, data processing pipelines, and moderate-scale web serving.
